title: init_seq
description: The asset-processing table's row-10 artifact ('IP programming guide -> init_seq.yaml: register write order and wait conditions -> directed test, connectivity check'). Authored as YAML (a real programming guide's init sequence is read and maintained by humans, and YAML keeps the step list reviewable); this schema validates the parsed document, so the same contract holds whether it arrives as YAML or JSON. INPUT CONTRACT, per the same discipline as register_map.schema.json: the ORDER and the WAIT CONDITIONS come from a real programming guide, never from an agent's guess about what a sensible bring-up order would be -- an invented init order is exactly the kind of plausible-looking content that produces a false PASS. What dv_harness/init_seq.py generates FROM this file is the Gate-2 precondition evaluation and the directed-test step list, not the sequence itself.

interface.description: The DUT interface this sequence brings up. Matches the names used in sys_regmap.json's governs_interfaces, so the two artifacts join without a translation layer.

steps.description: Ordered bring-up steps. Array order IS the required write order -- unlike register_map.schema.json's blocks array, where order explicitly carries no meaning.

index.description: Explicit ordinal, validated by init_seq.py to be contiguous and ascending so a step deleted during editing cannot silently reorder the sequence.

kind.description: write: program a register field. read_check: read back and require a value. wait_us: wait a documented settling time. wait_condition: poll until a field reaches a value, with a documented timeout.

block.description: Register block name, resolved against sys_regmap.json (or register_map.json) by init_seq.py -- never a bare address typed in by hand.

field.description: Field within the register; null/absent means the whole register.

value.description: Required for write and read_check and wait_condition; the value to write, expect, or poll for.

wait_us.description: Required for wait_us. A documented settling time from the programming guide.

timeout_us.description: Required for wait_condition -- a poll with no documented timeout is a hang, so the schema does not permit omitting it.
